deep_dive.title: Optimal-Access Cooperative MSR Codes: Parity-Check Matrix Construction And a Unified Transformation
deep_dive.abstract: Cooperative MSR codes are a kind of storage codes which enable optimal-bandwidth repair of any $h\geq2$ node erasures in a cooperative way, while retaining the minimum storage as an $[n,k]$ MDS code. Each code coordinate (node) is assumed to store an array of $\ell$ symbols, where $\ell$ is termed as sub-packetization. To address the disk IO (input/output) capability, a cooperative MSR code is said to have optimal-access property, if during node repair, the amount of data accessed at each helper node meets a lower bound on this quantity.   In this paper, we focus on reducing the sub-packetization level of optimal-access cooperative MSR codes. We propose new constructions of optimal-access cooperative MSR codes through two methods. At first, we propose a direct explicit construction by designing its parity-check matrix. Such parity-check matrix is built by repeatedly employing two crucial parity-check matrices as building blocks. Secondly, we propose a generic transformation framework. Starting from an arbitrary $[n+d-k,d]$ MDS scalar code, one can derive a final cooperative MSR code by systematically applying two basic transformations. Both approaches yield $(n,k,\ell=δ^m)$ optimal-access cooperative MSR codes with $δ=d-k+h$ and $m=\binom{n}{h}-\lfloor\frac{n}δ\rfloor(\binomδ{h}-1)$. Compared with the state of the art (with $\ell=δ^{\binom{n}{h}}$), the derived codes can reduce the sub-packetization $\ell$ by a fraction of $1/δ^{\lfloor\frac{n}δ\rfloor(\binomδ{h}-1)}$, where $δ=d-k+h$. Moreover, we also show that some previous code structures of optimal-access cooperative MSR codes and optimal-access MSR codes with $h=1$ are included as special cases of our transformation construction. At last, we note that all of the constructions are built over a finite field of linear size $\geq n+d-k$.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: This paper tackles the high sub-packetization cost of optimal-access cooperative MSR codes used for bandwidth-efficient repair of multiple node erasures in distributed storage. It proposes new parity-check matrix constructions and a unified transformation to build such codes with lower sub-packetization while keeping MDS storage and optimal-access repair. The results reduce sub-packetization and clarify code design trade-offs, aiding efficient erasure-coded storage repair.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 该文针对分布式存储中协作MSR码子分组过大、难以实用的问题，研究如何在保持最小存储与最优修复带宽的同时降低子分组化水平。作者提出基于校验矩阵的新构造以及一种统一变换，用以生成具备最优访问性质的协作MSR码。结果表明新构造在保持MDS存储与最优访问修复下显著降低了子分组化水平，为高效纠删码存储的节点修复设计提供了更可行的编码方案。

quick_skim.title: Binary Multiple-Node-Erasure-Correcting Codes over Complete Graphs: Constructions, q-Ary Metric Balls, and Duality
quick_skim.abstract: We study linear codes whose coordinates are the ordinary edges and self-loops of complete undirected graphs; a node erasure removes all coordinates incident with a failed vertex. The construction results are binary. For triple-node erasures, we extend the published cyclic construction by allowing a suitable cyclic check slope to depend on the prime graph length. An explicit determinant test proves that one of three fixed slope choices works at infinitely many prime lengths, unconditionally, and gives redundancy $3n-2$, one bit above the graph Singleton bound. We also give Singleton-optimal triple-node codes at $n=6,8,10,12$, together with a general ordinary-edge framework that isolates the remaining loop-completion problem. When $2$ is primitive modulo an odd prime $n$, a binary multi-slope construction corrects every $ρ$-node erasure for $2\leqρ<n$, with redundancy $ρn-(ρ-1)$ in the range $2\leqρ\leq(n+1)/2$. Returning to arbitrary prime powers, we derive exact generating transforms and inclusion--exclusion formulas for node-metric ball volumes, fixed-radius asymptotics, and packing, existence, and covering bounds. Finally, for the complementary clique-erasure metric, we obtain an exact weight enumerator and a Singleton-optimal node--clique duality.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: This paper studies linear codes over complete graphs where a node erasure removes all incident coordinates, aiming at storage systems that must recover from simultaneous node failures. It extends a cyclic construction for triple-node erasures by letting the check slope depend on the prime graph length, and provides a determinant test plus Singleton-optimal examples. The results give explicit redundancy bounds and a general framework for node-erasure-correcting storage codes.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该文研究以完全图边为坐标的线性码，节点擦除会移除该顶点所有关联坐标，对应存储系统同时多节点失效的恢复问题。作者扩展了三节点擦除的循环构造，令校验斜率随素图长度变化，并用行列式判别法证明在无穷多个素长度下可用，给出冗余3n-2。结果还给出若干达到Singleton界的构造与一般框架，为节点擦除纠正的存储编码提供了新构造与理论界。
